chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Sa'd, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about a Christian who became a Muslim, and with him was wine and pigs, and upon him was a debt. Can he sell his wine and his pigs so he can fulfill his debt? So he said: No.
ai.seo_question: Can a convert sell wine and pigs to pay debts?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) ruled that a newly converted Christian who possesses wine and pigs cannot sell these items to pay off his debts, implying that wine and pigs remain najasah (ritually impure) and are not fully transferable property for debt settlement in this context. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the intrinsic impurity of these items and their status as valid currency (mal) for discharging financial obligations, a nuance debated among scholars regarding whether the debtor must bear the loss or if the creditor accepts them in kind.
